title: Flood (simulation)
disclaimer: Simplified, indicative simulation run in your browser — not a certified hydraulic study. Nothing about the model leaves this device.
unsupported: This browser cannot run the simulation: it needs WebGPU, or WebGL 2 with float render targets.

ground.title: Ground
ground.order: Used in this order: the IFC's own terrain, an imported DEM, the map's relief, and the remaining holes filled from their neighbours.
ground.mapOff: Turn on the map with relief to use its terrain

buildings.title: Buildings
buildings.mapOff: Turn on the map to include the surrounding buildings

rain.title: Rain
rain.facts: {{mm}} mm over {{min}} min, peaking near {{peak}} mm/h. Uniform over the area.

stage.raster: Drawing the plan view on the GPU…

report.title: What the simulation sees
report.coarsened: The area is large for this cell size: cells widened to {{dx}} m.
report.planeWarn: No terrain data here: the ground is a plane at Y = {{y}} m. Import a DEM or turn on the map with relief for a real one.
report.coarseDem: The map's relief here comes from the global mosaic (≈30 m data): it does not see streets or kerbs. An imported DEM gives a better result.
report.canopyWarn: Most of the buildings read as raised (canopies): nothing reaches the ground under them, so water would run beneath. If this is one discipline of a federated set, such as the architecture model, load its structural model too (slabs, basement walls).
report.courtyards: Courtyards walled in by buildings: {{area}} m². They are taken as drained by their own gullies: no roof rain goes into them (the roofs drain to the street).

demNote.reprojected: The DEM was reprojected to the model's coordinate system.
demNote.sameCrs: The DEM is in the model's coordinate system.
demNote.assumedSameCrs: The DEM states no coordinate system (or the model does not): it is assumed to be the model's.
demNote.noHeightDatum: The model states no height datum: the DEM was stood on the project's ground floor under the model.
demNote.notGeoreferenced: The model is not georeferenced, so the DEM cannot be placed. Georeference it in the Map panel.
demNote.outside: The DEM does not cover the simulation area.

hyeto.label: Rain intensity per interval: press and drag to draw it

timeline.label: Flood timeline
timeline.probeHint: Click the scene to read the water there (Esc to stop)

probe.title: Probe
probe.hint: Click the scene to read the water at that point.
probe.obstacle: Inside an obstacle (a building): water does not enter here.

affected.title: Flood: elements reached
affected.summary: Below the highest water next to them: {{n}} of the {{checked}} elements checked.
affected.none: None of the {{checked}} elements checked (doors, windows, accesses, spaces, equipment) sits below the highest water next to it.
affected.partial: Maxima so far ({{t}}): the run has not finished.
affected.pending: Listed when the run finishes: doors, windows, accesses, spaces and equipment below the highest water.
affected.belowNote: Their bottom is below the ground outside (basements, sunken accesses). The figure is the water standing outside; whether it gets in depends on openings the simulation does not model.
affected.jump: Select it and fly to it
affected.note: Indicative: the water standing outside each element against its lowest point. Not part of the validation result or the Health Score.

export.title: Export
export.videoNeedsEnd: The video is available once the run has finished.
export.rasterNote: GIS files of the whole grid, north up; buildings are no-data. Depth in m, speed in m/s, arrival in s.
export.local: The model is not georeferenced: the file uses its local plan coordinates (metres), with no coordinate system.

capture.disclaimer: Simplified, indicative simulation: not a certified hydraulic study.

fit.raised: {{source}}: {{d}} m below the model's ground floor at the height its IFC states, so the model stood that high above the ground around it and no water there could reach its doors. The simulation's ground was raised to meet the model. Worth checking the IFC's height (IfcMapConversion.OrthogonalHeight).
fit.lowered: {{source}}: {{d}} m above the model's ground floor at the height its IFC states — the ground floor was buried. The simulation's ground was lowered to meet the model. Worth checking the IFC's height (IfcMapConversion.OrthogonalHeight).
fit.raisedOff: {{source}}: {{d}} m below the model's ground floor. As it is, the model stands that high above the ground around it, and the water there stays below its doors.
fit.loweredOff: {{source}}: {{d}} m above the model's ground floor. As it is, the ground floor is buried, and any water around it stands above its doors.
fit.switch: Stand the ground on the model's ground floor

data.map: The relief and buildings are the ones the map mode downloaded, with your permission, from public providers (relief: ICGC in Catalonia, GSI in Japan or AWS Open Data elsewhere; buildings: OpenStreetMap, through the Overpass API), which see the site's area and your IP address. The simulation only reads them: neither the model nor the results leave your browser. Turn both options off to simulate with the IFC alone; the permission is withdrawn in the Map panel.

osm.switch: Neighbourhood from OpenStreetMap: streets, parks, watercourses, walls
osm.mapOff: Turn on the map to read the neighbourhood
osm.title: Neighbourhood (OSM)
osm.counts: {{roads}} streets · {{green}} green or bare areas · {{channels}} open watercourses · {{oldCourses}} old or buried · {{barriers}} walls · {{buildings}} buildings
osm.oldCourse: A watercourse that is gone or buried runs here: {{names}}. It is not cut into the ground (filled in, or piped under the streets), but it is drawn as a dashed violet line: watch whether the water still finds it.
osm.failed: The neighbourhood could not be read from OpenStreetMap ({{message}}); simulated without it.
osm.partial: OpenStreetMap returned a partial neighbourhood (too many elements): some streets or buildings may be missing.
osm.fallback: OpenStreetMap was unavailable: the neighbourhood came from the map's tiles, without watercourses or walls. "Rebuild" asks again (at most once a minute).
osm.neighbourHint: Outlined on the map from amber (a few centimetres) to red (half a metre and more). Click one to fly to it.
osm.oldCourseWet: Over {{names}}: water stood on {{wet}} m² of its {{area}} m², up to {{depth}} m deep.
osm.oldCourseUnnamed: Watercourses that are gone or buried run here ({{n}}, unnamed in OpenStreetMap). They are not cut into the ground, but are drawn as dashed violet lines: watch whether the water still finds them.
